title: Hands Full
blurb: You come to the Last Anvil because the forges there never quite stop and people with iron on their palms speak plainly. The blacksmith shows you a hand-forged key kept under his bench and warns of a hatch in the wind-polished bedrock: go alone, take only what fits your hands, and be ready for reasons some would rather keep buried.

brief.premise: a secret lies in the desert

lore.title: Anvil and Dune
lore.premise: A secret lies in the desert: an iron hatch set flush in wind-polished bedrock, sealed by a pattern of hammer-scars that only a hand-forged key will fit. The village blacksmith keeps one such key under his bench and will tell any foot-traveller who asks that they will go alone, carry back only what fits their hands, and be prepared for a reason some people would rather the hatch stayed buried.
factions: Bell-Keepers (one family tied to the hatch lore)

1821480699.name: Anvil's Edge
1821480699.blurb: A wind-sculpted outpost where the village forge clamps the desert to a road of iron.
1821480699.culture: Hardpan folk who measure time by forge-fire and salt.
lore: The Forge keeps a salt-touched outpost at the bend where hardpan sighs into burnt hills.
The hatch key lies under a bench in the smithy; travelers are told they will go alone and return with only what fits their hands.
Bell-Keepers whisper of hammer-scar lore etched across wind-worn stones, guarding the hatch's memory.
Saltwardens patrol the dune-road, trading salt wind for stories but never the hatch's secret.
ambient: Heat blooms on the hardpan as noon tightens its grip.
Sparks rise from the anvil and scatter into brine-scented air.
Dunes rise behind burnt hills, a slow, patient horizon.
A Saltwarden's whistle rings out, urging boots to grit and pace.
Under the smithy bench, a hand-forged key remains dull with oil and ash.

1887326342.name: Hammerveil Highlands
1887326342.blurb: Wind-sculpted highland where a village forge guards an iron hatch buried in wind-polished bedrock.
1887326342.culture: Practical, iron-minded frontier folk who prize craft, road-keeping, and guarded memory.
lore: The hatch sits flush with bedrock beyond the highland, its hammer-scars aligned for a hand-forged key.
The Bell-Keepers guard the hatch lore; they speak of it only in winter’s breath.
The village blacksmith keeps a key under his bench and tells travelers to go alone, bring back only what fits their hands, and be prepared for a reason some would rather the hatch stayed buried.
Saltwardens patrol the road, keeping watch over miles and brine alike; they remember more than they say.
ambient: You crest a ridge; wind hisses, tasting of iron and ash.
You hear the forge breathe, a patient hammer-song from the village.
Dust lifts under your boots, clinging to leather as if kept in memory.
Saltwardens' pools glint along the road, briny and watchful.
Burnt hills loom on the horizon, red with old fires.

2817146631.name: Ironreach Sands
2817146631.blurb: Ironreach Sands hides an iron hatch in wind-polished bedrock, its edge lined with hammer scars that only a hand-forged key will calm; the Forge keeps that key under a bench, and the desert tests any who would unseal what some would prefer buried.
2817146631.culture: Hard-witted and wary, trades and beliefs knotted together under the sun.
lore: Saltwardens patrol the road to the town, noting every footprint that crosses from dune to settlement and exposing what you carry by the way you walk.
ambient: You set a boot on the hot hardpan; heat climbs your shin.
You study hammer scars gleaming on a distant rock, a code you cannot read.
You glimpse the hamlet's forge glow, a pale ember against the dunes.
You watch burnt hills fall into shadow, like old sentinels slept upright.
You approach the cave mouth at the dune's edge, listening for a breath in the dark.

3342859154.name: Anvilplain
3342859154.blurb: Wind-polished bedrock hides a hatch sealed by hammer-scar patterns, watched by a smith's hamlet.
3342859154.culture: Smiths temper iron against desert wind, Saltwardens keep the road, Duneborn wander, Bell-Keepers guard hatch lore.
lore: Anvilplain is carved by wind and sand where the bedrock lies bare; a hatch lies flush there, marked with hammer-scars that only a hand-forged key fits.
The village blacksmith keeps the key under his workbench, and tells travelers to go alone and return with only what fits their hands.
The Bell-Keepers guard the hatch lore; a family bound to its secrets for generations.
Saltwardens patrol the road to the town, keeping quiet about the hatch beyond a whispered name.
ambient: You step onto wind-polished bedrock; the sand threads through your boots.
Hammer-scar lines march across the rock, a map you can't read without a forge.
The Forge's smoke clings to your skin even if the hearth is cold.
Boots bite into the hardpan as dunes shift underfoot.
A distant bell from a cave—where the Bell-Keepers watch—tolls faintly at dusk.

1972728959.name: Anvilwatch Hold
1972728959.description: Dry air. The station sits on wind-polished bedrock where hammer-scar marks pace the desert’s memory. A hand-forged key rests under a bench, and a hatch beneath the rock waits for a traveler to meet its demand. The village’s temper is iron, the road’s line is long, and there’s a reason some are not eager for anyone to lift the hatch’s lid.

npcs.name: Nol Bannock
npcs.appearance: Sun-burnished, lean, with calloused hands.
npcs.persona: Grim and practical; quick with a question but not a lie.
knows: The hatch exists. The bedrock’s scars are real, and only a forged key will fit the hatch. The key lies under the smith’s bench, guarded by his word of silence.
You should go alone: the desert road is swallowing footprints and mercy is thin.
The road to the NE town has a route that avoids the dunes, but it’s longer and slower.

npcs.name: Garrick Ironhand
npcs.appearance: Broad-shouldered, soot-streaked apron, hands of iron and ash.
npcs.persona: Direct, blunt, protective of his craft.
knows: The key is under my bench. If you ask, I will tell you to go alone and to take only what you can hold in your hands.
The hatch wasn’t built by mortals alone; some say it’s older than the village and tied to the desert's first wind.
If you’re planning to actually go after it, be careful of what you owe to the wind.

npcs.name: Mara Thorne
npcs.appearance: Weathered face, linen apron, a broom always in one hand.
npcs.persona: Reserved, observant; uses travellers' gossip to barter for stories.
knows: The Duneborn caravans show up on windless days and disappear on good ones.
If you’re staying, keep your coins dry; a thirsty husband stole a map last winter.
There’s talk of a ghost of a key traded at the next town’s market, but no one can prove it.

npcs.name: Old Lira
npcs.appearance: Ragged robes, bell on a chain at belt, eyes sharp as a belled wind.
npcs.persona: Measured, patient; knows the lore of the hatch and its warding rites.
knows: The hatch’s lore is older than the village.
Patterns are forged; only the hammer-scar marks will guide a true hand.
Only a traveler who moves alone and returns bearing tools can begin to interpret the hatch’s mark.

npcs.name: Carvek of the Dunes
npcs.appearance: Cloth hood, worn leather, a pack of dried dates and small pots.
npcs.persona: Quiet, watchful; has seen more dunes than towns and trusts few people.
knows: The NE town’s caravan route is a known line; you’ll find the Saltwardens there.
Dunes remember every traveler who tested the hatch; some remember to forget you.
If you keep a promise, there’s a way forward you won’t forget.

npcs.name: Captain Teth
npcs.appearance: Laminar scar from a long road march, mail dented by wind.
npcs.persona: Grave, methodical; believes the road’s safety is a price paid in stories.
knows: The road’s been watched; there’s talk of a coastal caravan approaching the town to the northeast.
No one has unlocked the hatch’s secrets yet; hopeful hands rarely return with the truth.

hooks: The desert holds a hatch under bedrock; a hand-forged key will fit it, and only a traveler who goes alone should attempt it.
The blacksmith’s bench hides something else: a promise and a threat; if you seek the hatch, you may owe the village a debt beyond coins.

2165553418.name: Ironfold
2165553418.description: In the burnt hills of Anvilplain the wind-polished bedrock hides a hatch, its mouth sealed by hammer-scar patterns that only a hand-forged key will fit. The village watches the desert and the road: two roads meet here, a hamlet lies to the west and to the east, and a castle stands southwest. The smiths temper iron against the wind; the Saltwardens keep the road; the Duneborn wander; the

structures.name: Dry Dune Inn
structures.signText: Rest here, traveler; the desert forgets your name.

npcs.name: Tharic Ironbone
npcs.appearance: broad-shouldered, soot-streaked forearms, a ragged beard, eyes like flint
npcs.persona: dry, unflinching, speaks only when spoken to about the hatch
knows: There is a key under his bench. The hatch is sealed by hammer-scar patterns on bedrock; a hand-forged key will fit. Ask only once and mean it—some would rather

npcs.name: Marek Saltward
npcs.appearance: tall, weathered, thick boots, a crescent scar along his jaw
npcs.persona: laconic, vigilant, not inclined to chatter
knows: Two roads meet here; east goes toward the hamlet, west toward the castle ruins southwest. The hatch’s talk isn’t welcome, but if pressed he’ll say the smith

npcs.name: Jora Belmend
npcs.appearance: thin, silvered hair pulled back, a ring of keys at her belt
npcs.persona: precise, guarded, patient
knows: I guard hatch lore, and the hammer-scar pattern isn’t random. It aligns with a long-forgotten order. In the next town, a traveling smith called Mire might

npcs.name: Lysa Duneborn
npcs.appearance: dust-streaked apron, weathered face, quick, wary eyes
npcs.persona: watchful, weary, pragmatic
knows: Business is steady enough to cover rumors. A cloaked man passed through recently, asking for the key’s location. People in the east town speak of Mire the

npcs.name: Kran Jol
npcs.appearance: lean, copper rings on fingers, soot under nails
npcs.persona: sharp, calculating, fair with patience
knows: Prices are one thing; truth is another. The key sits under the smith’s bench, but duplication is a risk I won’t bear. A traveling smith in the next town named

npcs.name: Jarik the Gray
npcs.appearance: salt-worn hair, patched cloak, a stray dog at his heel
npcs.persona: curious, gossipy, observant
knows: Whispers from the well say the hatch isn’t just about treasure; it tests a person’s character. Some claim a hermit in the next town knows more than anyone

hooks: The smith will tell you, with a straight face and a misshapen grin, that you must go alone and bring back only what fits your hands, because some would rather the hatch stay buried.
There are rumors of a traveling smith named Mire in the next town who can forge a copy of the key if shown the right metal and the right symbol.

2227307379.name: Hammerwatch
2227307379.description: A highland hamlet where iron meets wind. A river runs by, two roads converge, and the desert’s secret lies pressed into wind-polished bedrock: an iron hatch sealed by hammer-scar patterns that only a hand-forged key will fit. The forge hums at the center, a Bell-Keeper’s Tower keeps watch, and the people move with the dry arithmetic of smiths and wanderers alike.

npcs.name: Garin Ironcleft
npcs.appearance: Soot-stained hands, lean frame, blue-gray eyes, wind-tousled hair.
npcs.persona: Dry, blunt, but reliable with a traveler who asks the right questions.
knows: Under my bench lies a key that opens the hatch in the desert bedrock; patterns hammered there must be matched by a hand-forged key.
If you ask, I’ll tell you the way to the hatch, but you will go alone and carry back only what fits your hands.
There is a reason some would rather the hatch stay buried; the thing beneath does not forgive easily.

npcs.name: Jorren Gatewarden
npcs.appearance: Wind-burnished face, jaw scar, mail crusted with sand.
npcs.persona: Dutiful, cautious, speaks plainly.
knows: Down the road to the east is the town where a mapmaker named Bren keeps charts of routes; he may sketch you a path to the hatch.
A caravan vanished last winter beyond the dunes; no one has heard from them since.
Saltwardens patrol the eastern road; travel at dawn or dusk at your own risk.

npcs.name: Nysa Underwell
npcs.appearance: Thin, shawled figure by the well; copper hair, eyes that miss nothing.
npcs.persona: Gossipy but wary; careful with what she repeats.
knows: The town to the east has a mapmaker who might know where the old paths lead; people pay him for routes and rumors.
No word has come from the caravan that passed here last winter; some say they found a riddle, others trouble.
If you head east along the road, you’ll meet a trader who still talks about the old gates and the hatch.

hooks: A hand-forged key lies under the smith’s bench, and the hatch in the desert waits for a lone traveller.
The hatch is sealed by hammer-scar patterns that only a skilled smith might recreate in the right metal.

3213465016.name: Bedrock's End
3213465016.description: Wind-swept hamlet at the end of the road. The Hammerveil Highlands loom over sand and low ground; the village forge guards an iron hatch buried in wind-polished bedrock. A hand-forged key sits under the smith’s bench, and the blacksmith will tell any traveler that they must go alone, carry back only what fits their hands, and be prepared for a reason some people would rather the hatch stayed

structures.name: The End of the Line Inn
structures.signText: End of the Line Inn. Bring only what fits your hands.

npcs.name: Gerran Ironhand
npcs.appearance: Stocky, soot-dark apron, hands stained with rust.
npcs.persona: Dry and blunt, but fair; he'll bargain for something unusual, but won't reveal the hatch's secrets easily.
knows: There is a hand-forged key under my bench.
The hatch behind the bedrock is sealed by hammer-scar patterns; it will yield only to a key that fits.

npcs.name: Ivar Croft
npcs.appearance: Lean, sunburned face, scar along the temple, weathered tunic and a wooden staff.
npcs.persona: Direct, measured, wary of outsiders.
knows: Greyport lies to the west; Calder the mapmaker there sometimes has older charts that hint at the hatch's approach.
The hatch is real. If you go, go alone, and only bring what fits your hands; some folks would rather the hatch stayed buried.

npcs.name: Mira Quill
npcs.appearance: Short, copper-haired, eyes quick and observant; patchwork but clean clothes.
npcs.persona: Gossip-prone but perceptive; careful with what she shares.
knows: Westward lies Greyport; Calder the mapmaker there has old charts that may show the hatch.
Rumor says the hatch's origin is known to mapmakers in Greyport; someone there might hold a map to its location.

npcs.name: Senn Hart
npcs.appearance: Lean, gray-bearded; patched coat; sits on a weathered crate by the road.
npcs.persona: Dry, laconic, but not unfriendly.
knows: The road to Greyport westward will take you past a caravan there; Calder the mapmaker keeps maps of old sites.
Greyport hasn’t heard from the mapmaker in months; if you want a map, you’d better move quickly.

hooks: A hand-forged key lies under the smith’s bench.
The hatch is real and sealed by hammer-scar patterns; it yields only to a correctly matched key.

3271006950.name: Hearthgate
3271006950.description: At the end of the road in the Hammerveil Highlands, Hearthgate sits on wind-sculpted ground where burnt hills press in from every side. The village is practical as an old iron tool: doors keep secrets, benches keep watch, and the furnace in the heart never cools. A whispered legend threads through the smoke: an iron hatch lies flush in bedrock, patterned with hammer scars that only a hand-forged

structures.name: The Dustbound Spoon
structures.signText: Go alone. Bring only what fits your hands.

npcs.name: Garan Coalbeard
npcs.appearance: Stout, soot-streaked apron, hands gnarled by iron and heat.
npcs.persona: Dry, precise, blunt; the sort who measures trust in inches of metal and truth in steel-gray eyes.
knows: The hatch's key sits under my bench; whispered to travelers who ask the right questions.
The hatch is sealed by hammer scars, pattern of five marks; only a hand-forged key will fit.
Some folks would rather the hatch stay buried; they want the desert to forget whatever lies beneath.

npcs.name: Borin Halbeard
npcs.appearance: Lanky, wary, iron-gray beard, cloak patched with desert dust.
npcs.persona: Cautious, curt, speaks in clipped sentences; he drinks no promises.
knows: The road beyond the village runs southeast toward Dalcrest; there are iron-workers there who know things.
Ask too much about the hatch and you’ll get a weather eye and silence; the desert keeps its own counsel.
If you want real knowledge of what’s down the road, talk to Nier the Mapmaker in Dalcrest; he’s the one worth finding in the next town.

npcs.name: Mira Duskdown
npcs.appearance: Wrinkled skin, hair in a wiry halo, a threadbare shawl, always leaning on the well’s rim.
npcs.persona: Quiet observer; she lets the water do the talking, but she notices when strangers carry more questions than coins.
knows: The well tastes faintly of iron most days; it knows your footsteps before your mouth moves.
The hatch’s legends drift along the road; the desert keeps its memory, and someone hasn’t spoken in a while—the hermit Ivar along the ridge.
Dalcrest isn’t far; talk to Nier there if you want a map of what lies ahead; he’s the kind of man who collects truths and scars.

npcs.name: Edda Mirth
npcs.appearance: Short-cropped hair, apron always damp with soot and meal; eyes quick with calculation.
npcs.persona: Protector of travellers who pay their way; wary of those who have empty pockets and bigger promises.
knows: The Dustbound Spoon is a place to wait for the next road’s real face; travellers come and go with stories and bruised knuckles.
If you’re after the hatch’s truth, Dalcrest’s mapmaker is your best bet; the road to the next town is rough but honest.
I hear Ivar the hermit has not been seen for months; some say he lies beyond the dunes, others say he never left.

npcs.name: Joran Crag
npcs.appearance: Broad-shouldered, hands always dusty with wood and sweat; wears a clasped leather belt.
npcs.persona: Blunt, good-humoured, tries to point people toward work and word at once.
knows: The ridge road splits near the bend; there’s a hermit named Ivar who’s worth seeing if you want to know what nobody has heard from in a while.
Dalcrest again is a place to seek a map and a traitor to memory; Nier the mapmaker has more eyes than most.
If you’re chasing the hatch’s past, you’ll need more than courage; you’ll need iron and a plan that a smith could respect.

npcs.name: Tilda Sone
npcs.appearance: A thin silhouette with a soft voice; lines in her face like grain in iron.
npcs.persona: Quietly stubborn; she remembers the old days and never waste a moment on vanity.
knows: The village holds its own stories; the hatch is a memory pressed into bedrock, waiting for a key with a master’s touch.
What’s down the road is not a destination but a test of character; the next town holds men who’ll lie and glaze over truth, or tell it straight.
I once spoke with a hermit who spoke to the road itself; he hasn’t spoken in a long while.

hooks: The blacksmith has a key under his bench; he will tell a traveler who asks to go alone and bring back only what fits their hands.
The hatch is sealed by hammer scars; a hand-forged key fits the pattern, and some people would rather the hatch stay buried.

3287834627.name: The Last Anvil
3287834627.description: A town where sun-scorched sandstone meets iron-smoothed grit. The Forge sits at the heart, its keeper guarding a key and a secret that desert-worn feet come to tempt. One road, the end of the line; a cave yawns to the southwest; every exchange here is a calculation, every rumor a spark.

structures.name: The Dry Well Inn
structures.signText: Rest here, if you dare the road’s echo.

structures.name: The Dune Ledger
structures.signText: Accounts settled by dust and time.

npcs.name: Garth Ironhand
npcs.appearance: Iron hands, soot-streaked leather apron, eyes pale blue.
npcs.persona: Terse, unyielding. Speaks in plain terms and no-nonsense; he’ll lay out the hatch mystery if pressed but only in guarded increments.
knows: There is an iron hatch in bedrock, hidden behind the desert’s glare. A hand-forged key sits under my bench. If you mean to unseal it, go alone, bring back only

npcs.name: Rin Tel
npcs.appearance: Tall, sun-darkened, scar along a stiff jaw.
npcs.persona: Measured, watchful, quick to caution outsiders; speaks softly but with a tilt toward menace when he suspects lies.
knows: Beyond the gate lies a road twisting toward Dustveil. A trader came through last moon with a map that contradicts the hatch story. The desert tests those who

npcs.name: Mara Cinder
npcs.appearance: Dust-darkened hair, a quick smile that doesn’t reach her eyes.
npcs.persona: Dry humor, steady host; she size-ups travellers and then prices their tale.
knows: Lodging costs a copper or two; travellers gossip on the road. The hatch rumor threads through every night’s firelight, though most keep to whispers.

npcs.name: Vess Dune
npcs.appearance: Lean, copper-skinned, patched leather, eyes always scanning.
npcs.persona: Brisk, plainspoken, trades coins as easily as words, rarely reveals more than needed.
knows: The Dune Ledger trades with caravans and carries word from towns beyond the ridge. There’s talk of a map to the next town that doesn’t match the hatch’s tale.

npcs.name: Juno Kest
npcs.appearance: Older man, weathered face, sits on a bench with a half-smoked pipe.
npcs.persona: Quiet observer, collects rumors and shadows; well-traveled without leaving town."
knows: Rumors say a trader vanished near the southwestern cave; some say he owned a map the hatch would answer to. The road east to Dustveil? It’s not linear; the

npcs.name: Nara Wisp
npcs.appearance: Small, keen-eyed woman with herbs tucked behind her ears.
npcs.persona: Soft-spoken, precise, with a calm that makes you forget you’re in a sun-scorched plain.
knows: The desert’s air will burn you if you linger, but the cave to the southwest glows pale green at night. If you’re unsealed there, bring water and a reason.

hooks: The hatch exists as a lone test against a traveler—go alone, take only what fits your hands, and be prepared for a reason some would rather the hatch stay buried.
A caravan-mason’s map rumored to have crossed Dustveil hints at a route that doesn’t coincide with the hatch’s pattern—follow it or beware the desert’s tests.

4064606860.name: The Last Anvil
4064606860.description: Wind gnaws at iron and heat. A road ends here, and the forge keeps the desert at bay with a sustained hiss of heat and sparks. A secret lies buried in bedrock beyond the dunes: a hand-forged key sits under a shop bench and the hatch it fits has stumped more than one passerby. Those who seek it are warned to go alone, to carry back only what fits their hands, and to be prepared for a reason some

structures.name: Under the Bench
structures.signText: The key sits under the bench; speak to the smith if you

structures.name: The End of the Line Inn
structures.signText: Beds for the road's end. Leave behind what you cannot carry.

npcs.name: Garik Ironhand
npcs.appearance: Broad-shouldered, soot-streaked hands, a beard crusted with metal dust.
npcs.persona: Direct and terse; values a straight answer and a fair exchange.
knows: The hand-forged key sits under my bench. It’s real. I’ll tell you nothing more unless you mean to walk away and not look back.
The hatch is sealed by hammer scars—patterns you’ll recognize if you know iron as well as I do. You’ll need a key made with the same fire.

npcs.name: Lina Brighteye
npcs.appearance: Sunburnt skin, scarf tied tight, eyes always weighing a traveler’s baggage.
npcs.persona: Warm enough to draw you in, cautious enough to count your coins before you sit.
knows: The road east leads to the next town, where a caravan still slips through at dusk.
Some say a visitor once opened the hatch and vanished; the next town over is where the whispers start again. If you want routes, talk to the caravan master

npcs.name: Rook Vale
npcs.appearance: Tall, lean, a scar along one cheek and eyes that miss nothing.
npcs.persona: Calm, wary, and precise; he reads a traveler fast and won’t be hurried.
knows: The cave to the northeast is real and not for the reckless. Paths there are rough, and the desert plays tricks.
Someone tried to pry open something there a few months back; they never returned. If you’re going that way, keep your wits and your steps quiet.

npcs.name: Sera Moss
npcs.appearance: A thin figure with sun-creased skin, hair in a loose braid, always near the well.
npcs.persona: Light, talkative, collects rumors as if they were coins.
knows: The NE cave holds more than echoes. A hermit used to haunt the entrance and speak in parables about iron and time.
No one has heard from the hermit in months. Some locals think he left for good; others say the desert has him now.

npcs.name: Marn Quickheel
npcs.appearance: Jumpy, always fidgeting, patched clothes and quick hands.
npcs.persona: Gossipy, nimble with words, always selling a story to the next traveler.
knows: The next town isn’t far if you know the dune paths, but watch the wind—it will flip your map and your memory.
The blacksmith in the next town is said to trade with the desert; he’ll know more about the key’s exact place and who’s been asking about it.

npcs.name: Kiva Thorne
npcs.appearance: Slim, patient, eyes that seem to measure the room before anyone speaks.
npcs.persona: Observant, quiet, and patient enough to wait for the right moment to speak.
knows: The hatch isn’t just metal and stone; it’s a test of intention, designed to sift seekers from dreamers.
There’s a reason someone would bury something in this desert—protecting something too dangerous to walk free. The NE cave’s old tales mention a keeper who

hooks: The blacksmith has the hand-forged key, but he will speak to a traveler who goes alone and carries nothing that could be left behind.
Hammer-scar patterns around the hatch match exactly the type of scars you’d leave on a forge for a key that will fit only a certain lock.

arc.title: Hands Full
arc.premise: You come to the Last Anvil because the forges there never quite stop and people with iron on their palms speak plainly. The blacksmith shows you a hand-forged key kept under his bench and warns of a hatch in the wind-polished bedrock: go alone, take only what fits your hands, and be ready for reasons some would rather keep buried.

quest.name: A Blessing to Turn
quest.description: Garik says the temple custodian keeps a narrow iron ward she will hand over to anyone who asks. Bring it back if you want the comfort of a blessing before you try the hatch.

beats.journal: Garik let me see where the key sits and told me the rules. He asked if I would fetch a ward from Kiva; it can be refused.

quest.name: Read the Bell-map
quest.description: Recover the rolled bell-rub hidden in the Bell-Keeper’s Tower at Hammerwatch and return it. The rubbing marks the hatch and repeats the old admonition: carry only what fits your hands.

beats.journal: I took the road to Hammerwatch and found a bell-rub up in the Bell-Keeper’s Tower. The faint letters only repeat the warning about what you can carry.

entry.text: Word travels from Garik’s bench to Hammerwatch’s square: the ward from Kiva can be refused, but the price is never spoken aloud.

sections.heading: What has changed
sections.body:
Dawn finds the tower door ajar, a pale draft slipping up the stairs.

The faint letters that warn what you can carry drift with every gust, and the rule to go alone begins to murmur at the edge of sight.

The desert presses against the doorway with the stubborn patience of hammered iron, and the hatch beneath the bedrock waits for a reason that will not yield to hunger or fear.

entry.text: A lone traveler slips away from Hammerwatch at dusk, leaving behind only dust and a silence that weighs like a suggestion of rain.

barriers.lockedText: The hatch remains shut. It will not yield without a reason that fits a hand and a memory of the desert.
barriers.opensText: When that reason arrives, the hatch will rise and reveal what waits beneath the bedrock.

item.name: rolled bell-map
item.description: A bell-rubbing on stiff cloth; the drawing shows the hatch's hammer-scar pattern and a single warning scrawled in salt: 'Take only what fits your hands.'

greeting.speech: Road ends here. Forge keeps the sand off the iron. Say plain.

choices.text: I'm after the hatch in the dunes.

tell-key.speech: If it's the hatch you mean: I keep a hand‑forged key under my bench. Go alone. Carry back only what fits your hands. The hatch is sealed with hammer‑scar patterns—you'll need a key made in the same fire, and be ready; some things folk prefer buried.

choices.text: Let me see where it sits.

under-bench.speech: There—under the second board. I don't hand it over without a promise. Before I give it, fetch a ward from Kiva; she marks small things so the hatch won't turn wrong.

choices.text: I won't run errands for strangers.

explain-ward.speech: Kiva keeps the bell by the east well. Old woman, spends mornings rubbing metal and saying names. Take her something small; she'll mark it with a ward. It's not praise—it's a precaution.

accept.speech: Good. Kiva's hut is left of the well. Here—keep the key close. Bring her ward back before you pry at rock. No packs, no coin piles; just the key and your hands.

actions.note: Bring Kiva's ward before opening the hatch.

revisit-open.speech: You already saw where it sits. Still want it or not?

choices.text: Yes — I'll fetch the ward from Kiva.
